trial.title: Comparison of In-Home Versus In-Clinic Administration of Subcutaneous Nivolumab Through Cancer CARE (Connected Access and Remote Expertise) Beyond Walls (CCBW) Program
indication: Clinical Stage II Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma AJCC v8
Clinical Stage IIB Cutaneous Melanoma AJCC v8

Clinical Stage III Cutaneous Melanoma AJCC v8

endpoints.measure: Change in patient-reported rating of Cancer CARE Cancer Connected Access and Remote Expertise (CARE) after 8 weeks
endpoints.time_frame: At baseline and up to 24 weeks of in clinic or at home care
endpoints.description: Measured using the Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (CAHPS) Cancer Care Survey assessing "your overall cancer care experience," answered on a scale of 0-10 where 0 is the worst experience possible and 10 is the best experience possible. The change in patient-reported rating of Cancer CARE after 8 weeks of in clinic care to the same rating after 8 weeks of at home care will be compared.
The proportion of patients who prefer care at home or express no preference will be computed and compared with the proportion of patients who prefer care in the clinic.

endpoints.measure: Patient level of comfort with receiving injections at home
endpoints.description: The proportion of patients who express comfort will be tabulated and a proportion greater than 70% will signify acceptance. Likert patient feedback questions and "Was It Worth It" questions will be described using frequencies and relative frequencies by arm. Numeric analog scale questions will be described using means and standard deviations and compared within patients (if applicable) using paired t-tests. Descriptive estimates at 24 weeks (after 8 weeks of in clinic and 16 weeks of at home care) will be generated throughout.

Patient-reported symptoms will be measured using the Patient Reported Outcomes Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (PRO-CTCAE). In this study, PRO-CTCAE items were chosen based on common symptoms experienced across cancer patients and side effects common with nivolumab. A free-text item will also be included for patients to report other symptoms as willing. Adverse events (AEs) will be tabulated during the 8 weeks in clinic, and during the 8 weeks at home, compared between arms and summarized over the 24 weeks.

Assessed using the European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Function 17 (EORTC QLQ-F17), a 17-item patient-reported questionnaire about patient ability to function, overall health and quality of life, and perceived financial impact of cancer and its treatment. The first 15 questions are answered on a scale of 1-4 where 1=not at all, 2=a little, 3=quite a bit, and 4=very much. The final two questions (overall health and overall quality of life during the past week) are answered on a 1-7 numeric analogue scale where 1=very poor and 7=excellent.

endpoints.time_frame: After 8 weeks of in-clinic and 8 weeks of at home care
endpoints.description: Assessed using the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy (FACIT) - Item GP5, "I am bothered by side effects of treatment," which is answered on a scale ranging from 0 (Not at all) to 4 (Very Much). Responses will be computed and compared across patients visits. Mean GP5 scores over time will also be explored.

endpoints.time_frame: At 8 weeks of in-clinic and 8 weeks at home care
endpoints.description: The maximum grade for each type of AE will be summarized using Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0. The frequency and percentage of grade 3+ AEs will be reported and compared using McNemar's test.

endpoints.time_frame: At 8 weeks of in-clinic and at 8 weeks of at home care
endpoints.description: The proportion of patients with an emergency room visit or hospitalization will be computed and compared using McNemar's test. Proportion of patients with emergency room visits or hospitalizations will also be summarized over the entire study.

endpoints.time_frame: Up to one year post study completion
endpoints.description: OS is defined as the time from study entry to death from any cause. OS will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.

outcome.rationale: Pilot trial designed to evaluate feasibility and patient experience of home-based subcutaneous nivolumab. Primary endpoint (CAHPS improvement) likely positive based on home care preference literature. Key secondary endpoints (patient preference >70%, comfort >70% threshold) expected to meet success criteria. Safety endpoints should demonstrate non-inferiority to clinic administration. Trial success defined by meeting patient experience benchmarks rather than clinical efficacy.

value.effect_measure: mean change in CAHPS rating (0-10 scale)
value.estimand: within-patient change from 8-week in-clinic to 8-week at-home period, single-arm paired analysis

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: No direct evidence for CAHPS change with home immunotherapy; extrapolated from general home care satisfaction literature and subcutaneous nivolumab acceptability data
value.rationale: Home administration eliminates travel burden and clinic waiting time, expected to improve patient experience. CAHPS cancer care scores typically range 7-9/10; modest improvement (1-2 points) plausible. CheckMate 8KX showed subcutaneous nivolumab well-tolerated. Confidence limited by lack of direct comparative evidence.

value.effect_measure: proportion preferring home or no preference
value.estimand: proportion of patients expressing preference for home care or no preference vs clinic preference at 24 weeks

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: Based on general home infusion preference literature; no specific data for subcutaneous immunotherapy in this population
value.rationale: Home infusion consistently preferred by cancer patients when safety assured. Convenience, reduced travel time, and comfort of home environment drive preference. Study selects patients willing to participate in home-based care, further biasing toward home preference. Conservative estimate: 65% prefer home, 10% no preference, 25% prefer clinic.

value.effect_measure: proportion expressing comfort with home injections
value.estimand: proportion of patients expressing comfort with receiving injections at home at 24 weeks, threshold >70% for acceptance

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: Threshold-based endpoint (>70%); patient selection and home health nurse support increase likelihood of meeting threshold
value.rationale: Study designed with home health nurse visits and remote monitoring, addressing key safety concerns. Patients must have Wi-Fi and live within 35 miles, selecting for those with resources and proximity for emergency response. Subcutaneous administration is less invasive than IV. Expected comfort rate 75-80%, exceeding 70% threshold.

value.estimand: change in patient-reported symptoms comparing 8-week in-clinic vs 8-week at-home periods

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: No direct evidence for symptom differences by administration location; symptoms primarily drug-related not location-related
value.rationale: PRO-CTCAE symptoms primarily reflect nivolumab adverse effects (fatigue, rash, diarrhea) rather than administration setting. No mechanistic reason for symptom differences between home and clinic. Slight trend toward fewer symptoms at home possible due to reduced stress, but effect likely small and not statistically significant. Prediction: minimal difference, uncertain direction.

value.estimand: improvement in function scores from baseline to 24 weeks, higher scores indicate better function

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: Limited evidence for QLQ-F17 specifically with home immunotherapy; extrapolated from general home care QoL improvements
value.rationale: EORTC QLQ-F17 assesses function, health, and financial impact. Home administration reduces travel burden and time away from work/family, potentially improving function scores. Financial impact may improve due to reduced travel costs. Effect size modest (2-point improvement on multi-item scales) given stable disease population on maintenance therapy.

value.estimand: mean GP5 score after 8 weeks in-clinic and 8 weeks at-home, lower scores indicate less bother from side effects

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: GP5 scores primarily reflect treatment side effects rather than administration setting; minimal difference expected
value.rationale: GP5 item ('bothered by side effects') correlates with objective AE rates rather than care setting. Nivolumab side effect profile similar regardless of SC vs IV or home vs clinic. Slight reduction in bother at home possible due to comfort of familiar environment, but effect small. Prediction: stable scores ~1.7-1.8 (moderate bother), no meaningful difference by setting.

value.estimand: proportion of patients with grade 3+ AEs during 8-week in-clinic vs 8-week at-home periods, compared via McNemar's test

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: Based on CheckMate 8KX safety data for SC nivolumab; home administration with remote monitoring should not increase serious AE risk
value.rationale: CheckMate 8KX established SC nivolumab safety profile comparable to IV. Grade 3+ AEs with PD-1 inhibitors typically 10-20%. Home administration includes home health nurse visits and remote monitoring, maintaining safety oversight. No mechanistic reason for increased AEs at home. Prediction: similar rates in both settings (~14-15%), no significant difference by McNemar's test.

value.effect_measure: proportion with ER visits or hospitalizations
value.estimand: proportion of patients with ER visits or hospitalizations during 8-week in-clinic vs 8-week at-home periods

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: Limited data on ER/hospitalization rates specifically for home immunotherapy; extrapolated from general oncology emergency rates
value.rationale: ER visits/hospitalizations in oncology patients typically driven by disease progression, infection, or treatment complications rather than administration setting. Home health nurse presence and remote monitoring provide safety net. Study eligibility excludes high-risk patients (ECOG 0-1, no uncontrolled comorbidities). Prediction: low rates (~7-8%) with no meaningful difference between settings.

value.estimand: median OS from study entry up to one year post study completion, Kaplan-Meier method

group_predictions.group_label: Health services research (in-clinic and at-home nivolumab)

value.uncertainty: Heterogeneous population with multiple tumor types; OS primarily driven by underlying disease rather than administration setting
value.rationale: OS varies widely by tumor type: melanoma (median 20-30+ months with nivolumab), NSCLC (12-18 months), RCC (20-30 months), ESCC (10-15 months). Mixed population with adjuvant and metastatic settings. This is a health services research trial; OS is exploratory endpoint. Administration setting (home vs clinic) not expected to impact survival. Prediction: median OS ~18 months for mixed population, wide confidence interval due to heterogeneity.

analysis_trace.trial_identification: NCT06265285: Single-arm Phase 2 pilot trial comparing in-home versus in-clinic subcutaneous nivolumab administration through Cancer CARE Beyond Walls (CCBW) program. 50 patients, multiple solid tumor indications.
analysis_trace.indication: Multiple advanced/metastatic solid tumors including melanoma, NSCLC, RCC, ESCC, HCC, urothelial carcinoma, SCCHN, MSI-H/dMMR CRC. All indications where IV nivolumab is FDA-approved.
analysis_trace.patient_population: Adults (≥18 years) with ECOG 0-1, multiple tumor types, receiving subcutaneous nivolumab via home health nurse visits with remote monitoring. Residence within 35 miles of clinic with Wi-Fi required.
analysis_trace.target_mechanism: Subcutaneous nivolumab (PD-1 inhibitor) administered via home health nursing with remote patient monitoring. Primary focus is health services research evaluating patient experience, not efficacy/safety of drug itself.
analysis_trace.endpoint_interpretation: Primary endpoint: Change in CAHPS Cancer Care Survey rating (0-10 scale) comparing 8 weeks in-clinic vs 8 weeks at-home. Secondary endpoints: patient preference, comfort level (>70% acceptance threshold), PRO-CTCAE symptoms, EORTC QLQ-F17 function, GP5 side effect impact, grade 3+ AEs, ER visits/hospitalizations, OS.
analysis_trace.safety_analysis: Subcutaneous nivolumab safety profile expected similar to IV formulation based on CheckMate 8KX study. Grade 3+ AEs typically 10-20% with PD-1 inhibitors. Home administration with remote monitoring should not increase serious AE rates.
analysis_trace.key_risks: 1) Limited direct evidence for this specific home administration model; 2) Patient selection bias (requires Wi-Fi, proximity to clinic); 3) Single-arm design limits causal inference; 4) Small sample size (n=50) for preference/comfort endpoints; 5) Multiple tumor types may introduce heterogeneity in patient-reported outcomes.
analysis_trace.evidence_to_prediction: Evidence from CheckMate 8KX (subcutaneous nivolumab PK/safety), general home infusion literature showing patient preference for home care, and CAHPS survey validation in cancer care support positive patient experience outcomes. No direct evidence for CCBW program specifically.
analysis_trace.coverage_gaps: No published results from NCT06265285 available. No direct evidence for CAHPS score changes with home vs clinic subcutaneous immunotherapy. Limited evidence on emergency room/hospitalization rates specifically for home-based immunotherapy administration.
